{"docs/MEMORY_PROVIDERS.md":"# Storage-independent memory providers

Harness defines logical memory and its epistemic rules. A conforming host chooses
one canonical provider, authorizes access and coordinates publication. Any host
can implement this contract without a particular host product, package, service,
command, layout or downstream release. Inference remains external.

Phase A retains the existing JSON/Git implementation and adds a supported public
record API. There is no new database dependency, automatic migration or promise
that larger JSON graphs are now supported.

## Public boundary and versions

Hosts may import these **packaged, public ES modules** from an unchanged installed
Harness. Node 22.12+ is required. Imports from other implementation modules are
private unless separately documented. No package-manager installation is needed.

| Module | Supported exports |
|---|---|
| `server/memory-contract.mjs` | `memoryContract`, `collections`, `canonical`, `digest`, `bytesDigest`, `matches`, `tokens`, `assertProvider`, `pages`, `records`, `get`, `evidenceBytes`, `changeIdentity` |
| `server/provider-memory.mjs` | `createMemory`, `semanticWrites`, `rebaseChanges` |
| `server/provider-validation.mjs` | `validateSnapshot`, `validateCandidate`, `snapshotDigest` |
| `server/memory-transfer.mjs` | `exportMemory`, `importMemory` |
| `server/cognitive-reference.mjs` | `createProviderReadView` |
| `adapters/reference-git/adapter.mjs` | `createAdapter`, including `openMemory({instance_id})` |
| `adapters/reference-json/provider.mjs` | `createJsonProvider`, `createJsonTransferReceiver` for an explicit transactional host store/sink |
| `adapters/template/memory-provider.mjs` | Application-owned provider scaffolding |
| `adapters/conformance/provider-suite.mjs` | `providerConformance(name, factory)` |

| Version dimension | Current | Refusal rule |
|---|---|---|
| Logical memory | 2; hypotheses 1 | Reject unsupported records/formats before writes; never reset/reanalyze |
| Provider / semantic changes / portable stream | 1 | `assertProvider` / `changeIdentity` / import refuse unsupported combinations |
| Host module integration API | 2 | Public modules and transactional callback obligations below |
| Physical JSON format | graph 2 + optional provider sidecar 1 | Only the reference adapter interprets it |
| Existing reference adapter CLI | 1 with `memory-provider-v1` capability | A new standalone cycle must request the capability when claiming |
| Cognition task/result | 1 | Unchanged; consumes `createProviderReadView` |

Required provider capabilities: `record-reads-v1`, `paged-evidence-v1`,
`semantic-changes-v1`, `candidate-isolation-v1`, `portable-export-v1`.
Version numbers do not imply one another. A provider must advertise only behavior
it actually supplies. Absence or incompatibility refuses explicitly.

## Ownership and complete state inventory

| State / responsibility | Authority | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| Entities, claims, graph source descriptors | Harness semantics; provider storage | Canonical transactional `entities`, `claims`, `sources` records; stable IDs, exact sources, retained corrections |
| Original observations / indexed evidence | Host intake; Harness provenance | Canonical `observations` descriptors and paged exact source bytes; derived evidence indexes are retained artifacts |
| Processed ledger | Harness completion meaning; host transaction | Canonical `processed` records, atomically coupled to the candidate and receipt |
| Questions / answers / analysis | Harness | Canonical `questions`, with stable wording, source identity and analyzed closure |
| Hypotheses / uncertainty / premises | Harness | Canonical `hypotheses`; evidence must resolve in the same snapshot |
| Events, cycle journals, verification pointers | Harness meaning; host durability | Canonical `events`, `journals`, `verification`; append-only records, resolvable pointer pairs |
| Publication receipts | Host durability, Harness identity fields | Canonical `receipts`, atomically published with completion; never inserted after a separate successful commit |
| Older journals, events, learning receipts and auxiliary files | Existing semantic format retained | Immutable `artifacts` with stable IDs, original locator and exact bytes; existing historical pointers remain resolvable |
| Purpose, selected profile, vocabulary / retained guidance | Application supplies content; Harness defines precedence | Snapshot-pinned `policy` and identity; original configuration/text and retained run guidance are exported as artifacts |
| Read models / Markdown summaries | Host/backend | Derivative reference presentation, regenerated at completion/import; never substituted for canonical records |
| Lease/reservations, authorization, credentials, endpoint/configuration | Host | Not portable knowledge; recheck under the publication lock; no leases are imported |
| Snapshot ancestry, retention, CAS, transaction/WAL, locks and reconciliation | Host/provider | Opaque snapshot identity; history and source bytes remain snapshot-bound |
| Merge | Harness semantic intent; host freshness | `rebaseChanges` checks touched-record digests and policy; host owns ancestry and the next lease |
| Admin, backup, provider selection/switching, cutover and deployment | Host | Explicit host procedures outside this contract; no Harness migration workflow |
| Export/import | Harness invariants; host staging/durability | Paged canonical records + exact source chunks; validate in isolation before atomic archive publication |
| User request/answer schemas, learning authorization | Existing cognition contract | No duplicate task lifecycle; see `COGNITIVE_TASKS.md` |

A canonical provider serves one authorized instance scope. Scope is fixed when
constructed; `instance_id`, snapshot selectors and query filters cannot grant
access. Agent input cannot select a module, connection string or authorization
policy. Providers may share an implementation, but must isolate scopes.

## Provider operations

All methods except `describe()` may be asynchronous. Return copies, never mutable
references to committed state. Collections are listed by `collections` in the
contract module. Operations never accept a graph object, graph filename, SQL or
Git argument. Observation `path` is retained **logical provenance** from the
existing observation format, not an instruction to read a backend file.

| Operation | Request / response | Required semantics |
|---|---|---|
| `describe()` | Versions and capabilities | Explicit negotiation; physical format is informational |
| `open({snapshot?})` | Metadata: `instance_id`, `snapshot_id`, `logical_version`, `updated_at`, `policy_id`, `policy` | Omitted snapshot selects current committed state; returned handle immutable |
| `read({snapshot,collection,id})` | `{status:'found',record}` or `unknown` / `unavailable` | Exact ID only; unknown is absence in this snapshot, unavailable is a retention/access failure, never negative evidence |
| `scan({snapshot,collection,selector,purpose,limit,cursor})` | `{items,next_cursor}` | At most 100 rows per page; stable ID ordering; exhaust every matching physical candidate; never silently apply top-k |
| `counts({snapshot})` | Counts by collection | Counts, not record bodies; no lease required |
| `evidence({snapshot,id,offset,max_bytes})` | `status`, `base64`, `total_bytes` | Raw source byte ranges, 1..65,536 bytes; offsets are bytes; missing retained bytes are unavailable |
| `prepare({change,writes,change_digest})` | `{candidate_id,snapshot_id}` | Verify `semanticWrites`; immutable isolated overlay; no committed state or completion change |
| `publish({candidate_id,change_digest,candidate_digest})` | Durable receipt, optional new `snapshot_id` | Independently validate the exact candidate and all host fences under one transaction |
| `abort({candidate_id})` | Aborted status | Discard draft/handles; leave committed state untouched; safe repeated abort |
| `recover({idempotency_key})` | Original durable receipt or null | Receipt is authoritative even after response loss or process restart |

`selector` supports AND-combined `ids`, `refs` (OR references), `group`
(`subject_id`, `predicate`), `external` (exact scheme, namespace, value), and
normalized `tokens` (OR). The shared `matches` function defines physical matching.
It does not choose winners, merge identities or interpret facts. `purpose` is an
operation label (`lookup`, `query`, `validation`, `audit`, `export`), never an
authorization grant. Ordinary exact lookups use filtered selectors. Audits,
statistics and broad queries may enumerate pages. A host can enforce quotas by
refusing explicitly; it cannot return a falsely complete partial match set.

Cursors are opaque and bind snapshot, collection, selector, operation purpose and
scope. Reuse with a different binding refuses. Draft snapshots cannot be used as
committed snapshots. Aborted drafts expire immediately. Committed snapshots stay
valid while retained by the host; pruning makes handles/cursors explicitly
unavailable/expired, never aliases them to current state. The JSON/Git reference
supports retained ancestors of the selected instance branch; it does not promise
retention after host Git garbage collection or history rewriting.

## Retrieval and validation

`createMemory(provider)` supplies `open`, `read`, `source`, `context`, `stats`,
`warnings`, `audit`, `prepare`, `publish`, `abort`, `recover`. Lookup/ranking,
scoped external identity, current/valid-time selection, dependencies and conflict
meaning remain Harness decisions. Physical candidate queries retrieve complete
correction/temporal groups **before** output bounds. Current ties and alternatives
remain explicit; aliases and identical names do not establish identity. Source
reads are separate and snapshot-bound. Context is bounded to existing output
limits; warnings state their scope and truncation. `warnings` performs a complete
paged warning audit; it is not restricted to the context top-k.

Validation uses point reads for references/evidence, paged record audits, and
complete dependency/correction topology checks. It does not validate only the
retrieved subset. Candidate validation in this first implementation performs a
full paged audit, including previous-record history, rather than claiming
incremental validation performance. The pure in-memory ranking/statistics helpers
remain internal working-set implementations, not a mandatory provider boundary.

The JSON backend still parses/scans/materializes full files. Paged APIs remove
the physical-format requirement; they do not eliminate JSON costs, change logical
capacity limits, increase the Git reference's 64 MiB child-output envelope, or
establish support for a 100 MB graph. Broad neighborhoods can still be expensive.

## Semantic changes and publication

A change has `provider_version:1`, opaque `base_snapshot`, `policy_id`, `lease_id`,
`run_id`, `attempt_id`, `idempotency_key`, UTC `at`, `sources:[{id,sha256}]`, and
`operations`. It contains semantic intent, never replacement graph files.

| Operation | Fields / rule |
|---|---|
| `add_entity`, `add_claim` | `record`; ID must be new; canonical logical record schema applies |
| `extend_entity` | `id`, optional `aliases`, `source_ids`, `external_ids`; additions only |
| `set_claim_status` | `id`, `status`; active to superseded/retracted; old content retained |
| `put_question` | `record`; wording/source identity retained; closure needs analyzed evidence |
| `put_hypothesis` | `record`; premises must exist, confidence/uncertainty semantics preserved |
| `append_event` | `record` with ID, reserved `observation_id`, `question_id`, `answer`, `answered_at` |
| `append_journal` | `record` with run ID, pinned `policy_id`, semantic `review`, `model`, `verification_id` |
| `append_verification` | `record` with attempt ID, `run_id`, `result`; retain observed configuration/limitations as needed |

Sources are completed by the host transaction, not a model-supplied processed
flag. Exactly one host candidate assembly component writes completion records:
`semanticWrites` derives CAS-bound record writes and one processed/source row per
claimed source, preserving prior records. The agent supplies semantic operations
and source identities; it must not also append completion rows. The provider's
isolated candidate must contain these records before validation. A logical
provider need not expose `processed.json` or filesystem staging. Audits reject
duplicate IDs (`processed: duplicate/invalid ID`) separately from source integrity
failures; records are never silently deduplicated.
Every cycle requires a journal and separate resolvable verification record, even
if the verification result is a qualified or limited result. A deterministic
fixture must never claim actual-model evaluation.

| State | Allowed transition / effect |
|---|---|
| Committed snapshot + owned lease | Prepare isolated candidate; no committed draft leakage |
| Prepared | Audit against base; compute canonical candidate digest; errors abort |
| Validated | Publish only after independently rechecking everything below |
| Published, response delivered or lost | Recover the original receipt by idempotency key; do not reprocess sources |
| Prepared / validated but interrupted before CAS | No receipt/completion exists; retry or rebuild an attempt |
| Aborted / expired | Candidate handle refuses; committed knowledge stays intact |

Publication must serialize against host writers and independently recheck:
base freshness, lease ownership/expiry and reservations, exact source identities
and bytes, pinned policy, semantic-write digest, full candidate validity/history and exact correspondence to `semanticWrites`,
and candidate digest. The exact validated candidate, source completion, lease
release and receipt must commit atomically. A caller's previous validation is
insufficient. A provider must not expose a partial commit or successful receipt
before its durable commit point. Host writers must use the host's coordination
protocol; editing live backend files bypasses that protocol and requires
intervention. The reference detects dirty source/policy/protocol/output files at
its fences and reconciles local files/index after committed response loss.

The digest covers the candidate's logical records, pinned policy and exact source
bytes. The publication envelope appends its own receipt atomically; the receipt
contains the pre-envelope candidate digest, avoiding a circular self-hash. Prior
receipts are immutable candidate content. The returned `snapshot_id`, when
present, is a physical-provider handle assigned at commit; the stored receipt
identity is the idempotency key and digest, not a fabricated future Git SHA.
A recovery result never pretends that a later current head is the original
publication snapshot.

An identical prepared retry returns the same candidate. Conflicting use of an
idempotency key refuses. After publication, `prepare` tells callers to recover;
`publish` on a retained candidate returns its original receipt. After candidate
loss/restart, recover by key, then open a fresh committed snapshot. Providers must
check source/policy/lease/freshness again even if validation previously passed.

`rebaseChanges(provider, change, newSnapshot)` compares all touched prior-record
hashes and pinned guidance. Conflicting edits or duplicate source completion
refuse. It does not infer ancestry, merge identities or publish. Abort an old
prepared attempt before rebasing; the host reviews/rebinds the next attempt and
lease. The legacy directory merge tool remains a JSON-reference utility.

## Standalone JSON/Git use

Initialize a new external instance once and commit it to its own attached-branch
repository as described in `ADAPTERS.md`. Never reinitialize existing knowledge.
The following launcher explicitly selects the reference backend:

```sh
node processor/provider-tool.mjs claim --instance /private/instance --instance-id my-instance
node processor/provider-tool.mjs context --instance /private/instance --instance-id my-instance --snapshot SNAPSHOT --request context-options.json
node processor/provider-tool.mjs apply --instance /private/instance --instance-id my-instance --request semantic-changes.json
node processor/provider-tool.mjs recover --instance /private/instance --instance-id my-instance --key cycle-key
```

Claim returns the snapshot and immutable guidance. A provider-capable claim
captures reserved original source bytes in the committed intake snapshot. Use the
returned base/policy/lease/source identities when producing semantic changes.
`apply` prepares, validates and publishes in one process; it never asks an agent
to generate a workspace graph or supply `--previous`. `open`, `stats`, `warnings`,
`audit`, `rebase` and streaming `export` are also supported. Evidence paging is
available via the public module API. CLI request paths are launcher inputs, not
fields in the provider-neutral contract.

For a host integration:

```js
import {createMemory} from './vendor/golem-harness/server/provider-memory.mjs';
const memory = createMemory(hostAuthorizedProvider);
const snapshot = await memory.open();
const context = await memory.context(snapshot.snapshot_id, {entity_id:'ent-example'});
const candidate = await memory.prepare(hostReviewedSemanticChanges);
const receipt = await memory.publish(candidate);
```

Host-owned providers import the public validators; they do not copy/fork private
semantic code. `createProviderReadView` connects a provider to the existing
cognition task/result protocol. The old `createMemoryReadView({state,...})` helper
is JSON fixture support; it is not the required host integration boundary.

## Portable export/import and migration prerequisites

`exportMemory(provider, snapshotIds)` yields a checksummed stream: versioned
manifest; each snapshot's original identity, pinned metadata and logical digest;
paged logical records; exact evidence chunks; snapshot ends; final checksum.
Canonical JSON sorts object keys, retains array order and uses exact JSON
scalars. Record order is stable by ID. Each event extends a SHA-256 checksum
chain; logical digests compare record IDs/content and exact evidence independently
of physical snapshot/instance identity.

`importMemory(stream, receiver)` requires an isolated host receiver with `begin`,
`snapshot`, `record`, `evidence`, `seal`, `publish`, `abort`. It verifies the chain,
stream/snapshot scope, source chunk sequence, full semantic audit and logical
equivalence before calling `publish` once. Duplicate records, missing evidence,
corruption and incomplete streams fail with staging discarded. Receivers retain
multiple snapshots, IDs/history, original source hashes, pinned policy, receipts
and journal/verification pointers. Imported snapshot IDs are new; the sink must
retain a durable original-to-imported snapshot alias map for old citations and
receipt references. It must not claim physical identity equality. Old provenance
locators remain metadata, not required physical paths for another provider.

The independent record receiver is a contract fixture. The JSON receiver restores
JSON-origin archives, including the original guidance/configuration artifacts,
into an explicit host archive sink. It does not invent missing JSON configuration
for an arbitrary provider's policy representation. Refuse unsupported imports
instead. The host supplies atomic staging/archive durability; no provider is
switched and no active instance is overwritten by these functions. Backups,
cutover/reverse migration and any optional future database implementation remain
host responsibilities.

## Conformance and retained evidence

Run `node --test adapters/conformance/provider.test.mjs`. The same suite exercises
the JSON/Git reference and an independent record-map provider/minimal host.
The latter has no graph/file/Git dependency and rejects unfiltered ordinary
lookups. Fault controls cover pre/post-publication interruption, stale base,
source/policy drift, lease expiry, candidate seals, retries and lost responses.
The test provider is not a production database.

New vendors can call `providerConformance(name,factory)`. The factory returns
`provider`, `reserve(change)`, `expire()`, `changeSource()`, `changePolicy()`,
`advance()`, `interrupt('before'|'after')`, and `reopen()` for isolated synthetic
instances. Its initial logical corpus is `providers/corpus.mjs`. Fault controls
are trusted test seams, never model-loaded hooks.

The package builder includes/runs these tests, the existing regression suite and
installer checks. Supported platform CI retains observed job results; unrun or
pending platforms are not claimed as passing. See `MEMORY_PROVIDER_ACCEPTANCE.md`.
No host-specific issue, migration or release blocks Harness acceptance. Actual
LLM conformance is tracked separately in `COGNITIVE_CONFORMANCE.md`.
","docs/MEMORY_MODEL.md":"# Source-grounded memory model (0.7.0)

The graph is version 2. It contains sources, entities and claims. Sources preserve
UUID, inbox path, exact UTF-8 SHA-256 and recorded_at. Every processed ledger row
must resolve to a graph source and vice versa. Entities have an opaque ID, coarse
type, label, aliases, source_ids, created_at, uncertainty and optional stable kind.
Claims use attributed_to_id and classification source_assertion, hypothesis or
corroborated. Entity-valued objects represent relations; scalar objects represent
values. There is no automatic truth evaluation or semantic embedding service.

Only the target format is supported. Previous runtime/instance formats may be
scrapped and recreated with the initializer. No legacy reader, alias conversion,
layout migration or rollback workflow is provided. Historical release documents
remain historical evidence, not setup instructions for this version.

The physical paths and graph-file procedures below describe the JSON reference.
Other [memory providers](MEMORY_PROVIDERS.md) enforce the same logical schemas,
evidence and history rules through records, without requiring these files.

## Provenance and history

Each claim cites exact nonempty body quotations. Subject, attribution and object
entities must include every cited observation in their source_ids. asserted_at
copies a cited source's recorded_at exactly; it is not an upstream authoring date.
valid_time represents evidenced effective time, with explicit precision. Recording,
upstream assertion and validity time must not be conflated.

Within a target-format instance, retain source identity/bytes and old claims.
Retained claim fields (including depends_on) are immutable except status. Correct
through new claims and supersedes; do not reactivate superseded/retracted claims.
Entity type, stable kind, created_at, retained source IDs and external IDs are
protected. A changing domain category is a claim, not a mutation of stable kind.

## Scoped external identifiers

An entity may have up to 64 external_ids, each {scheme, namespace, value}. Scheme
is a lowercase slug; namespace and value are nonempty trimmed strings (500/1000
characters maximum). Identity is the exact triple, including case. No implicit
URL/path normalization, suffix extraction or commit-hash abbreviation is performed.
Identifiers are append-only. Aliases and labels do not establish equivalence.

Exact lookup uses separate arguments to avoid ambiguity with colons in namespaces:

```sh
node processor/memory-tool.mjs context --root ../instance --external-id 1001 --scheme record --namespace https://synthetic.invalid/catalog
```

A query matches exact identifier values or configured prefix+value forms, as whole
whitespace-delimited tokens (or the entire query for values containing spaces).
Declare prefixes in a vocabulary v2 file. A bare value matching several scopes
returns alternatives, never an automatic merge. duplicate_external_id warns when
two entities share the same scoped key. Distinct namespaces do not collide.

## Temporal retrieval

Declare single_valued predicates in vocabulary v2. context --current true selects
active claims per subject/predicate before output truncation and graph expansion.
Exact effective starts no later than evaluation time outrank partial/as-reported
bounds and recording-time snapshots; alternatives remain explicit. Partial or
as-reported bounds use valid_time.from_uncertain only when no exact start is
available, with unresolved=true. Expired intervals and future starts are not current. If no known
start exists, latest asserted_at is a labelled asserted_at_heuristic, not proof of
current truth. At the latest time all tied candidates are returned, subject to the
output bound. current_selection records selection basis, selected IDs, alternative
IDs, unresolved state and alternatives_truncated; current_ties identifies differing
values with equal selection times. Other evidence is not erased or superseded.
Missing time/competing active values remain a review obligation.

context --valid-at 2026-01-15T00:00:00Z selects intervals whose known bounds contain
that time. Endpoints are inclusive; overlapping endpoints can return both claims.
A null bound is open; both bounds null or precision unknown is excluded and counted
in hidden.unknown_time. hidden.valid_time/current count other temporal exclusions.
Combining --current and --valid-at uses the supplied time for selection. This is
valid-time retrieval under the graph's current correction/retraction knowledge,
NOT reconstruction of what was known at a past transaction time. Explicit status
filters still apply; current single-valued selection uses active claims only.

## Hypotheses and dependencies

memory/hypotheses.json is strict JSON with schema_version 1, updated_at and a
hypotheses array. Each record requires id, statement, status, support, refutation,
confidence and updated_at. Optional confidence_basis/model are bounded strings;
observation_ids references graph sources. Status is open/supported/refuted/withdrawn;
confidence is 0..1 and is an analyst assessment, not a calibrated probability.
supported requires support; refuted requires refutation. Empty arrays are valid
for open/withdrawn. IDs are unique within the collection. Record timestamps cannot
exceed the collection timestamp. Support/refutation IDs must resolve to claims.

Malformed JSON names the file. Missing/unsupported version, invalid shape, unknown
claim/source IDs, out-of-range confidence, duplicate hypothesis IDs and unsupported
status are errors, also during adapter candidate validation. No legacy warning-only
mode exists. validateHypotheses diagnostics include the resolved path and record ID
or schema path: hypothesis claim not found, hypothesis source not found, duplicate
hypothesis ID, hypothesis updated after collection, hypothesis status needs evidence.

Claims may list at most 128 unique depends_on claim IDs. Missing, self-referential
or cyclic dependencies fail. Iterative topology validation is O(V+E) and stack-safe.
Exact source quotation and entity provenance remain mandatory. Direct dependencies
on superseded/retracted evidence produce dependency_changed for active claims and
open/supported hypotheses, naming both IDs. Support and refutation changes both
matter. This does not change conclusion status/confidence, propagate truth or do
unbounded transitive review. Reverse-impact retrieval is not added in this release.

## Retrieval and resource bounds

The deterministic CLI validates the full target snapshot before context/stats.
Lexical normalized tokens, aliases, values and source quotes seed ranking; optional
predicate/type/kind/status filters and up to three graph hops are available.
Related-claim expansion uses the temporally selected graph, never reintroducing an
excluded claim. No match is not proof of missing evidence: pending inputs and
unfetched records are outside processed knowledge.

Output is at most 100 claims, 100 primary entities and 100 source records; supporting
entities close returned claim endpoints. Source excerpts have a 4,000-character
per-source and 64,000-character total budget, with explicit truncation. These
excerpt limits do not truncate exact quotations embedded in the returned claims;
use a smaller claim limit when quotations themselves are large. Follow the
original citations before drawing conclusions from excerpts. expansion_budget is
at most 20,000. Sources have 10,000 slots, entities 5,000, claims 20,000; each claim
has at most 32 source quotations. Profiles cannot raise engine limits.
stats.capacity derives used/limit for each collection from the schema. Near-limit
warnings start at ceil(80% * limit). Exceeding a limit fails before publication.
See CAPACITY_BENCHMARKS.md for measurement, platform and byte-size limitations.

## Validation before publication

Validate a complete proposed snapshot including ledger and hypotheses against the
committed prior graph, then publish atomically through the storage adapter. Keep
lease ownership and compare-and-swap; re-read/revalidate after concurrent changes.
Do not manually rewrite RELEASE.json or bypass checks in a consuming application.
The schema checker accepts only its bundled bounded keyword vocabulary.

Completion rows have one writer: the host candidate assembler (the adapter/backend
when it owns assembly). Cognition agents do not also append rows on adapter or
provider paths. Direct staged-file validation requires the host to supply all
rows first; it does not generate them. Logical providers use processed records,
not a mandatory `processed.json` file. See the
[responsibility table](PROCESSING.md#completion-row-ownership).

## Validation rules

Schema diagnostics include the failing graph path and describe shape, type, value
or schema vocabulary violations. The following messages describe cross-record
checks in `validateMemory`. Unsupported fields such as `speaker_id` fail schema
validation as `unexpected field`; unsupported classifications fail as `invalid enum`.
There is no alias-coexistence attribution check in graph v2. The CLI additionally checks that the readable queue
contains each question's ID and text.

| Diagnostic | What to check |
|---|---|
| `duplicate ID` | Each source, entity or claim ID is unique within its collection. |
| `Entity/claim ID collision` | Entity and claim IDs must be distinct. |
| `Invalid question queue` | Supply a version 1 queue with a questions array. |
| `Invalid/duplicate question` | Supply unique valid question IDs, a supported status and nonblank text within the length limit. |
| `Question source missing` | The question's source observation must exist. |
| `Question analysis source missing` | Every observation referenced by question analysis must exist. |
| `Closed question needs an analyzed answer` | A closed question requires answered analysis with source observations. |
| `Invalid processed ledger` | Supply a version 1 ledger with an observations array. |
| `Duplicate processed row` | Exactly one completion row is allowed per observation ID; fix the candidate assembler, never silently deduplicate. |
| `Ledger source mismatch` | Each row must have status `processed`, an existing source and matching source path and hash. |
| `Processed source missing from graph` | Each ledger source must be represented in the graph. |
| `Graph source mismatch` | The graph source path, hash and timestamp must match the inbox observation. |
| `Graph source is not processed` | Stage a matching processed ledger row for every graph source. |
| `Invalid source` | Verify the observation ID, filename, nonempty body and parseable recording time. |
| `Unknown source question` | A source's question reference must resolve in the queue. |
| `Entity source missing` | Every entity source ID must resolve to a graph source. |
| `Entity created after graph update` | Entity creation must be at or before the graph update. |
| `Claim entity not found` | The named `subject_id`, `attributed_to_id` or `object.entity_id` field must reference an existing entity. The message includes both IDs. |
| `Claim source/quote mismatch` | Every cited observation must be a graph source and contain the exact quote. |
| `Entity provenance does not include claim source` | The subject, attributed entity and entity-valued object must each include every cited observation ID in their own `source_ids`. |
| `Hypothesis requires uncertainty` | Supply uncertainty for any hypothesis. |
| `Invalid time range` | The validity start must be at or before its end. |
| `Unknown time cannot assert bounds` | Unknown validity has empty bounds. |
| `Exact time needs a bound` | Exact validity requires a start bound. |
| `Claim created after update` | Claim creation must be at or before the graph update. |
| `Assertion timestamp must match a source` | Copy `recorded_at` from any cited observation to `asserted_at` exactly, including its fractional-second formatting. |
| `Invalid correction` | The older claim must exist, differ in ID, share the subject and predicate, and be superseded or retracted. |
| `Missing replacement claim` | A superseded claim needs a replacement that references it. |
| `Correction cycle` | Correction links must be acyclic. |
| `Graph update timestamp went backwards` | Preserve or advance the prior graph update timestamp. |
| `Entity identity/history removed` | Retain each prior entity's ID, type, creation time and source IDs. |
| `Claim history removed` | Retain every prior claim. |
| `Claim history mutated` | Preserve all prior claim fields except status. |
| `Claim status history reversed` | Preserve the status of every already superseded or retracted claim. |
| `Source history changed` | Preserve every prior graph source record. |
| `Invalid/duplicate external identifier` | External IDs are trimmed and unique by scheme/namespace/value. |
| `Entity external identifier history removed` | Retained external IDs cannot be removed or changed. |
| `Unsupported/invalid previous graph` | Prior graph must use the target schema and valid shape. |
| `Invalid claim dependency` | Every dependency exists and differs from the claim itself. |
| `Claim dependency cycle` | Dependency edges must be acyclic; cyclic IDs are named. |
| `Readable queue missing question` | Include the question ID and text in the Markdown queue. |

Provider validation independently enforces unique IDs in each logical collection:
`processed: duplicate/invalid ID` rejects repeated completion IDs before checking
source integrity. It does not accept or silently deduplicate malformed records.
The JSON duplicate diagnostic above is specific to `validateMemory`.

## Validation warnings

Warnings are advisory and have code, object_id, message and documentation.
CLI validate/adapter completion return at most 1,000 warnings with warning_summary
(total/returned/truncated); large duplicate/conflict messages show the first ten
IDs plus the omitted count. The library collector returns the complete list. They
prompt review; no absence of warnings proves truth or independent corroboration.

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `unused_entity` | Entity is not referenced by claims. |
| `duplicate_corroboration` | Corroborated claim cites identical source bodies; repetitions are not independence. |
| `unknown_kind` | Stable kind is not declared in the selected vocabulary. |
| `unknown_predicate` | Predicate is not declared in the selected vocabulary. |
| `unknown_external_id_scheme` | Identifier scheme is not declared by the selected vocabulary. |
| `duplicate_external_id` | Exact scoped identifier belongs to more than one entity. |
| `multiple_active_values` | Single-valued subject/predicate has different active objects; equal repeated values do not warn. |
| `dependency_changed` | Direct support/refutation/dependency evidence was superseded/retracted. |
| `capacity_near_limit` | Source/entity/claim usage is at least 80% of its engine limit. |

Hosts may add namespaced advisory warnings at their boundary. Policies cannot
weaken schema, quotation, history, identity or transaction rules. No executable
warning hooks, total evidence-strength ordering or automatic truth scores exist.

## Unknown hypothesis confidence capability

`hypothesis-unknown-confidence-v1` adds explicit `confidence:null` (unknown) with uncertainty retained in `confidence_basis` and the proposal to hypotheses v1. Numeric confidence keeps its meaning.
Negotiate this capability before using newly generated reviewed-learning records;
older validators cannot validate null confidence. No source/graph migration is
needed. Cognitive task proposals and receipts retain rationale, verification and
correction history; see [COGNITIVE_TASKS.md](COGNITIVE_TASKS.md).
","docs/ANALYSIS_WORKFLOW.md":"# Profile-driven analysis and retrieval recipe

Use a fresh external target-format instance. The host provides permissions,
inference and storage; the engine remains read-only downstream.

1. Initialize an empty external root with processor/init-instance.py --root PATH
   --profile. State purpose, scope, language and review priorities in
   instance/purpose.md. Commit golem.config.json and all selected profile files
   together before a claim. An unconfigured instance has no domain policies.
2. Choose stable kinds and one predicate direction (for example parent_of rather
   than mixing parent_of/child_of synonyms). Keep changing categories as claims.
3. Write an explicitly selected vocabulary version 2. For a synthetic record:

```json
{"schema_version":2,"kinds":["record"],
 "predicates":["has_state","reports_result","verified_by","parent_of"],
 "single_valued":["has_state"],
 "external_id_schemes":[{"scheme":"record","prefixes":["REC-"]}]}
```

The selected config remains {"schema_version":1,"profile":{"path":
"profiles/default.md","vocabulary":"profiles/vocabulary.json"}}. These files
are in the external instance. JSON policy is declarative; prose is agent guidance.

4. Check adapter status/capabilities. The reference adapter advertises
   candidate-validation-v1, purpose-guidance-v2 and core-policies-v2. When selecting
   policies, require core-policies-v2 or a host-owned implementation with the same
   immutable guidance and validation semantics; do not silently use an old adapter.
5. Claim at most 20 aged, finalized observations. Read delivered guidance and keep
   the immutable snapshot/identity. Receipt of text does not prove adherence.
6. Retrieve before linking identities or writing claims. Exact lookup is preferable:

```sh
node processor/memory-tool.mjs context --root ../instance --external-id 1001 --scheme record --namespace https://synthetic.invalid/catalog
node processor/memory-tool.mjs context --root ../instance --entity ent-selected --predicate has_state --current true
node processor/memory-tool.mjs context --root ../instance --entity ent-selected --predicate has_state --valid-at 2026-01-15T00:00:00Z
```

Use actual opaque entity IDs from the first result, not ent-selected literally.
A raw question can be a poor lexical query; use identifiers and predicate filters.
Inspect ties, uncertain alternatives and truncation, and read full cited sources.
Zero hits do not establish absence: inputs may still be pending or unfetched.

7. Separate workflow state from a person's reported result and independently
   reviewed evidence. A Closed state is not a verification result. Record exact
   quotes and explicit uncertainty; neither duplicated source IDs nor repetitions
   establish independent evidence. Do not infer private/sensitive attributes.
8. Preserve retained claims. A correction for the same subject/predicate uses a new
   claim with supersedes and a terminal old status. For a changed predicate, retract
   the old claim and add the new claim; do not mutate its predicate. Add depends_on
   to a new conclusion when relevant; never edit it into a retained claim.
9. Review warnings and hypotheses every cycle. Keep missing-evidence questions in
   both queues; close only with reviewed source-grounded answered analysis. Optional
   host-owned closure_criteria metadata can guide review but is not a new core rule.
10. Stage graph, strict hypotheses, ledger, queues and journal in one candidate.
    Include guidance_version: ID from claim. Record completed local checks, mark
    host checks pending and select a durable completion-record pointer keyed by
    instance/run before validation (see [the pointer rule](PROCESSING.md#verification-record-and-journal-pointer-vi-019)).
    Then validate/commit via the adapter.
    On head conflict re-read/merge/revalidate; on committed policy change release
    and reclaim. Do not force another run's lease or mark pending sources processed.
11. Read back persisted state and retain the actual validation/publication/read-back
    results, snapshot identity and returned warnings at the selected location.
    Keep unresolved alternatives, questions and warnings reviewed in the staged
    journal; do not rewrite it after publication to add a verdict. Any candidate
    edit after validation requires revalidation. Resume from lease/ledger/run
    metadata; no reinitialization
    during ordinary processing. An incompatible old instance requires an explicit
    fresh setup, not an automatic conversion or deletion.

Manual hosts without delivered guidance must retain selected profile/config/text
and hash metadata themselves and verify deterministic policy checks. They may not
claim reference-adapter capability solely because they copied a recipe.

## Avoid cycle-specific scripts

The optional `processor/write-candidate.mjs` assembles graph/index/journal drafts
from a structured change set after semantic review. See PERFORMANCE.md. It does
not replace source indexing, hypothesis/question maintenance or the adapter
validate/commit sequence. Keep the selected profile concise and committed before
claim; do not rediscover domain conventions or generate transaction machinery
for each batch. Observe host process completion instead of fixed sleeps.
